audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup was built on an interaction that does not exist. Six fields (breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, mid, late, wants.foe[1], spikes[3].text) say Miasma's grounding stops Nautilus's Q gap-close or 'walls your Q reset'. Nautilus has no dash anywhere in his kit — Dredge Line is a thrown anchor — so the grounding does nothing to him, and the page had the player fearing the wrong half of the ability while standing in the poison. Separately, Petrifying Gaze was called a flat 'face-stun' with the actual rule never stated: it stuns only enemies FACING her and merely slows anyone with their back turned.
audit.why: These are the two facts that decide the lane. The thing that keeps Nautilus off her is Miasma's SLOW holding him outside his own 1150 hook range, not the grounding. And turning away from Petrifying Gaze converts her only hard CC into a slow — free counterplay that appeared nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Every grounding claim rewritten to name the slow as the real problem; Petrifying Gaze's facing rule written into spikes[1], phases[4].why, late and wants.foe[1]. Miasma's 24s rank-1 cooldown and Noxious Blast's 3.5s now carry the timing advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Cassiopeia all seven stages while every single why underneath says the opposite: whys[0] 'makes the trade favorable', whys[1] 'you can step up', whys[2] 'locks an escape-less Cass in place', whys[3] 'you control the wave', whys[4] 'your hardest spike', whys[5] 'still runs down a Cass'. Only whys[6] gives her the game.
audit.why: The prose, the 60% win rate and the early/mid blocks all describe a lane Nautilus wins until Cassiopeia's items land. The packet chart is ALSO wrong here — the packet flags itself ('chart contradicts data') and still lists Cassiopeia for six rows — so I took the chart from the prose rather than from the packet.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Nautilus for levels 1 through first item and Cassiopeia at 2+ items, in BOTH layers as matched pairs, with ratings rebuilt (6/10, 7/10 through the mid rows, 3/10 at the end). The generic phase whys that contradicted this were rewritten too.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named item timings but no cooldowns, and the level-6 spike credited the win to grounding immunity.
audit.why: Miasma's 24 seconds at rank 1 is the longest cooldown in her kit and the actual trade window; Twin Fang at 0.75s and Noxious Blast at 3.5s are why waiting her out does not work.
audit.corrected: 24s written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and phases[3].why; the level-6 spike rebuilt on Petrifying Gaze's facing rule instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemisation never mentioned Grievous Wounds despite Twin Fang healing her for a percentage of the damage it deals, on a 0.75s cooldown.
audit.why: Nautilus's plan is a shield-and-grind trade; Twin Fang healing off poisoned targets is exactly what beats that, and the missingInteractions file flags it.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now buys Bramble Vest against Twin Fang.

edits.before: Passive-root auto trades win the first exchanges. Identify how Cassiopeia contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Passive-root auto trades win the first exchanges, and Cassiopeia has no escape at level 1 — punish every last-hit she walks up for.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Miasma's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: Miasma is down 24s at rank 1, so trade inside that gap and bank leads. If ahead, freeze and deny her farm.

edits.before: Depth Charge is an unmissable point-click knockup — the all-in always starts. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cassiopeia's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Depth Charge is an unmissable point-click knockup — the all-in always starts. Petrifying Gaze only stuns if you face her; turn away and it is a slow.

edits.before: - Cassiopeia Miasma: matchup-defining — Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cassiopeia Miasma: 24s at rank 1 — the grounding does nothing to you, since no part of your kit is a dash; its SLOW is what holds you outside hook range. - Petrifying Gaze: turn away and it slows instead of stunning you.

edits.before: Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: The grounding does nothing to you — you have no dash. It is the slow that keeps you outside hook range.

edits.before: Track Cassiopeia's Miasma: Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it. When it is down — Hook + passive root chain.
edits.after: Track Miasma (24s): its grounding does nothing to a champion with no dash, but the slow does. When down — hook, passive root, Riptide chain.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (perma-slow chains), then Sunfire Aegis; boots Mercury's Treads.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet, then Sunfire Aegis; Mercury's Treads. Bramble Vest cuts Twin Fang's healing.

edits.before: Depth Charge is an undodgeable, grounding-immune lockdown — R or flash-Q a poisoned Cass and she dies, your hardest spike.
edits.after: Depth Charge is undodgeable lockdown and Miasma's grounding never touched it — R a poisoned Cass and she dies. Your hardest spike.

edits.before: She out-scales hard: with Liandry's and Rylai's she kites on her passive move speed, grounds your Q with Miasma, and out-DPSes your tank stats — concede the late game.
edits.after: She out-scales hard: her passive makes every move-speed buy count double, Miasma's slow keeps you outside 1150, and she out-DPSes your tank stats — concede late.

edits.before: Depth Charge is undodgeable lockdown that ignores her Miasma grounding — flash-Q or R into a poisoned Cass is a near-guaranteed kill, your hardest window.
edits.after: Depth Charge is undodgeable lockdown, and turning your back on Petrifying Gaze downgrades her stun to a slow — R a poisoned Cass and she has no answer at all.

edits.before: Once Cass has Liandry's/Rylai's she out-DPSes your tank stats, her Miasma walls your Q reset, and the R face-stun cancels your engage — she reclaims the lane.
edits.after: Once Cass has two items she out-DPSes your tank stats, Miasma's slow holds you outside your 1150 hook range, and Petrifying Gaze stuns you if you face her.

edits.before: Use Depth Charge at 6 to engage through her Miasma grounding and convert pressure to a kill or gank
edits.after: Use Depth Charge at 6 on a poisoned Cass — nothing in her kit dodges it — and convert to a kill or gank

edits.before: Keep poison ticking with Q and Twin Fang while kiting back on her passive move speed so you never land Dredge Line
edits.after: Keep Noxious Blast ticking every 3.5s and Twin Fang healing her off the poison, kiting so you never land Dredge Line

edits.before: Save Miasma to ground your Q gap-close and her R to face-stun your Depth Charge engage
edits.after: Save Miasma's slow to hold you outside 1150 and Petrifying Gaze for the moment you face her

edits.before: Levels 3 through 6 are your takeover — with Q, W and E up you win every short trade because your CC chain locks her in place and she can't kite what she can't outrun. Respect her Miasma: she'll drop it to ground your Q the instant you wind up, so bait it out or hook her from an angle the cloud doesn't cover. At 6, Depth Charge is undodgeable and ignores grounding entirely — flash-Q or just R a poisoned Cass and she dies, and this is your single best window to snowball before her items.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 6 are your takeover — with Q, W and E up you win every short trade because your CC chain locks her in place and she can't kite what she can't outrun. Respect Miasma for what it actually does: the grounding is meaningless against a kit with no dash, but its slow drags you out of your own 1150 hook range while the poison ticks. At 6, Depth Charge is undodgeable, and turning your back on Petrifying Gaze downgrades the stun to a slow — R a poisoned Cass and she dies.

edits.before: Be honest with yourself: once Cassiopeia hits two items she flips this lane hard. Liandry's and Rylai's let her DPS straight through your W shield and tank stats, her Miasma permanently walls your Q reset, and her R face-stun cancels your one engage. You have to kill her or get her so far behind in the early-to-mid windows that her scaling never matters — if she reaches full build even, you become a CC-bot who can't catch her.
edits.after: Be honest with yourself: once Cassiopeia hits two items she flips this lane hard. Item power lets her DPS straight through your W shield and tank stats, Miasma's slow keeps you permanently outside your 1150 hook range, and Petrifying Gaze stuns you the moment you turn to face her. You have to kill her or get her so far behind in the early-to-mid windows that her scaling never matters — if she reaches full build even, you become a CC-bot who can't catch her.

notes: The single biggest error: six fields told the player Miasma's grounding shuts off his Q gap-close. Nautilus has no dash in any slot, so the grounding is irrelevant to him and the real threat — the slow that keeps him outside Dredge Line's 1150 range while poison ticks — was never stated. The mirror audit found the same thing from Cassiopeia's side and calls it a recurring generic-Cassiopeia template error, so it is worth grepping the phrase across other matchups. Petrifying Gaze's facing rule (stun if facing, slow if your back is turned) was also completely absent and is now the level-6 counterplay. packet.suspectNames flagged 'Use Depth Charge' in wants.you[2] — FALSE POSITIVE, that is Nautilus's own R and the name is correct. The chart change here is Medium confidence, not High: the packet chart is self-flagged as contradicting the data, and the sample is only 5 games, so I built the chart from the seven whys and the early/mid/late prose, which are unanimous.
